mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of expected future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during periods of FEDFUNDS > 5%, or the inflation proxy CPIAUCSL does not show a concurrent rise.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2% coinciding with a falling UNRATE (unemployment rate) signals labor market strengthening, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% and UNRATE decreases in the same month
regime_hint: Early stage of labor market recovery
failure_condition: No significant positive return over 60 days when the trigger occurs, or the correlation between PAYEMS and UNRATE is not monotonic in the expected direction.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in both HOUST (residential construction) and GDPC1 (goods orders) exceeding 10% suggests weakening demand, which predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: both HOUST and GDPC1 decline by >10% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not significantly negative when the trigger is met, or the decline in HOUST/GDPC1 is not concurrent.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 5% while CPIAUCSL (inflation) remains below 3% indicates supply-side strength, forecasting a positive 20-day S&P 500 return.
regime_hint: Stable supply expansion in low-inflation environment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive when INDPRO > 5% and CPIAUCSL < 3%, or the effect is not robust across multiple inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 4% for three consecutive months, it creates a persistent liquidity premium that is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: No significant positive return over 60 days when FEDFUNDS stays below 4% for three months, or the effect is only observed during financial crisis periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% in a month with rising PAYEMS (>0.5%) indicates a tight labor market, predicting a positive 20-day S&P 500 return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% while PAYEMS rises by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return when the trigger is met, or PAYEMS does not rise while UNRATE falls sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in RSAFS (retail sales) above 3% accompanied by a decline in HOUST (<-2%) signals demand shift without supply response, predicting a negative 5-day S&P 500 return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >3% and HOUST decreases by >2% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not significantly negative when the trigger occurs, or the relationship reverses direction.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO and GDPC1 both show double-digit growth in the same month, it indicates robust supply expansion, which precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return in non-crisis regimes.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return when both INDPRO and GDPC1 grow >10%, or the effect is only present during supply shocks.
